written.text: Write a precis of the following passage by reducing to one third of its original length and give suitable title.(14) If a business activity does not require anything special to be done, it is not entrepreneurship. In fact a person cannot be called an entrepreneur unless he introduces something new, something different, in his venture. This is known as innovation, that is, doing something different from others. Entrepreneurs are constantly on the look out for something unique to fulfil the needs or wants of people. They may or may not be inventors of new products or new methods of production, but they are able to foresee the possibility of making use of an invention for business. Others who come to know about the same invention may not be capable of thinking about its practical usefulness in business, or they may not have the ambition or self-confidence to take advantage of it. In a competitive market, an entrepreneur can succeed only through innovation. Innovation need not necessarily be something big or dramatic. A simple adjustment to an existing product, providing service without extra charge, using colourful packaging, or selling a product in packets of different weights may all be profitable innovations. However, if similar things are done by many producers and sellers, entrepreneurs must think of other types of innovations. No wonder imagination is often more important than knowledge for innovative thinking. An entrepreneur must possess imagination as well as the ability to think creatively. Take the case of fruit juice. Nowadays fruit juice is sold in small cartons instead of bottles so that one can carry it easily and discard the container after use. This is an innovation. Let us consider another example. You may have heard of Henry Ford, who established the Ford Motor Company in the United States. He did not invent the automobile, but he applied new methods of mass production and produced passenger cars at low cost so that many people could afford them.
